- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment drops, forecast remains high for 2–3 days; adjust downward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or decay factor to reduce weight of last 5–7 days in forecast aggregation.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast to align with historical volatility patterns.
